question.text: 'Tapti Venture Fund I', a close-ended Cat I Venture Capital Fund, declared First Close on 1-March-2025 with committed corpus of INR 85 crore and Sponsor commitment in place. Which of the following statements about First Close is CORRECT?

answer.text: At the date of First Close, the corpus can be any amount agreed between Sponsor and investors
The Sponsor commitment can be withdrawn or transferred after First Close if replaced by new LP capital
At First Close, the corpus must not be less than INR 20 crore and Sponsor commitment cannot be reduced, withdrawn or transferred post First Close
First Close must be declared within 6 months from date of grant of registration; no extension permitted

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) Regulations: (i) corpus at First Close declaration must meet the INR 20 crore minimum; (ii) Sponsor commitment cannot be reduced/withdrawn/transferred post-First-Close. For LVFs, First Close must occur within 12 months of registration or PPM filing, whichever is later; tenure for Cat I/II starts from First Close date. The Trap: Option A ignores the INR 20 cr floor. Option B contradicts the Sponsor-commitment-lock. Option D has the wrong timeline — 12 months, not 6 months, for LVF; and regulation allows first close within 12 months from date of SEBI communication for PPM take-on-record. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests timing-of-close mechanics. XIX-C tests the Sponsor-lock and the 20 cr floor concurrently. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Build a 'First Close Conditions Precedent' checklist into the Fund Admin manual — bank account live, SCORES registration, Custody Agreement signed, FLA/FIRMS prep, NAV statement template. If First Close slips the 12-month PPM take-on-record window for LVF, the scheme loses LVF privileges.
